newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt rises with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt rises with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices rose in thin trading Thursday, led by an upswing in U.S. Treasuries prices and news that Venezuela would issue a 10-year Eurobond, traders said.

"Today the only story is Venezuela," a Brady bond trader said. "Venezuela has tightened by about 20 basis points, and that's really squeezing the life out of any short positions still left out there."

Venezuela plans to price a $315 million 10-year Eurobond via ING Barings in the next couple of weeks, market sources said. Debt analysts and investors projected the issue would price 275 to 300 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Late Thursday, Venezuela Pars were up 5/8 at 76-1/8 bid, and Discounts were up 3/4 at 87 bid.
Other countries' Bradys posted solid gains as well, traders said. Bracil "C" bonds were up 3/4 at 79-3/8 bid, and Argentina Pars were up 1/2 at 67 bid.

Gains in U.S. Treasuries provided much of the direction in emerging debt Thursday, market experts said. Treasuries climbed amid foreign buying and perceptions the U.S. economy may be slowing, U.S. analysts said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 20/32 to yield 6.98 percent.
"(Emerging market debt is) kind of directionless right now and just taking our cues from Treasuries," one trader said. "It's been pretty slow, with very little client activity."
The Corpus Christi holiday in Brazil and some European countries helped to restrain market activity.
